title: Shared shapes
description: The shapes more than one event, command or state field refers to. Anything used once lives next to its use.

Channel.description: The door the public came through: a phone call over SIP, the browser widget over WebRTC, or WhatsApp text.

Direction.description: Inbound: the public reached the agent. Outbound: the agent reached out (a dial).

EndReason.description: Why the call is over. Who hung up, what failed before anybody could, drained: the platform took the worker down (a deploy, a stop) with the call still on it, or app_detached: the app holding the agent closed its socket mid-call, so nothing was rendering the prompt or answering a tool — both are nobody's fault and neither is an error.

EndedBy.description: Whose action ended the call. platform covers timeouts, errors and a drained worker.

ScoreVerdict.description: What one judge answered about a finished call. Held: the rule held. Broken: it did not, and the reason names the evidence. Deferred: the judge was asked and could not settle it. Skipped: nobody asked it — no model was reachable inside the call's judging budget.

TransferMode.description: Cold: the caller is sent on and the agent leaves. Warm: the agent stays on the line until the other side answers, then leaves.

PromptRegion.description: Which region of the prompt a block lives in: static, before the history, cached by the provider; or dynamic, after the history, replaced every turn. The append-only history in between is never written by the app.

DocsMode.description: How the knowledge base reaches the model: retrieved, the platform runs search itself when the caller's turn ends; or tool, the model calls search when it decides to. Either way the chunks arrive as a tool result.

PlatformTool.description: The two tools the platform runs on the app's behalf: recall reads the contact's facts out of memory, search reads chunks out of the knowledge base. The app declares memory and docs and writes neither method; the platform runs the lookup, and the answer reaches the model as a tool result rather than as part of the prompt.

PromptBlockSpec.description: One named block of the prompt and the region it lives in. The default layout, when an agent declares none, is identity, knowledge and tools (static), then the history, then view (dynamic). A block's text is written per call with prompt.set.

name.description: The block's name, the one prompt.set writes it by: lowercase, digits and underscores.

UserState.description: What the platform believes the person on the line is doing right now. The states are the session's own.

AgentState.description: What the agent is doing right now, in the session's own words: warming up, waiting, hearing the caller, generating, or playing audio.

ParticipantKind.description: Who a participant is to the call: the person the agent serves (over SIP or the widget), the agent itself, a supervisor who took a seat in the room, a listener who only hears, or a second SIP leg that room.invite brought in.

TrackKind.description: What a track carries: a microphone's audio, a camera's video, or a screen share.

TrackSource.description: Where a track comes from, as livekit's TrackSource names it, in lower case.

EventSource.description: Where an outside fact came from: the tenant's backend over the app socket (app), or a participant's browser over the DataChannel (participant).

Visibility.description: Who may see a field of the app's state: everyone in the call (public), the tenant's own readers (tenant, the default for a field never declared), or nobody without masking (pii).

Projection.description: Which projection a sink applies before a state or an entry leaves the platform: public for a participant reading its own call, tenant for the tenant's readers. The contract is docs/protocol/projections.md; a client never applies one.

Contact.description: Who is on the line, as far as the platform knows. Everything is optional: a web visitor may be nobody yet.

id.description: The platform's own id for this contact, stable across channels and calls.

phone.description: The caller's number in E.164 form (+34 600 000 000 written as +34600000000).

name.description: The name the contact is known by, when memory or the app supplied one.

email.description: An e-mail address, when the web widget or the app supplied one.

external_id.description: The id the tenant's own system uses for this person, when the app told the platform.

Route.description: One door to an agent: a channel and, for phone and WhatsApp, the number that answers. A number is a route, never an agent.

number.description: The number in E.164 form for phone and WhatsApp; null for the web widget, which needs none.

label.description: A human name for the door, for the console: 'main line', 'after hours'.

Supervisor.description: The human who sent a supervise verb, as the token that let them in names them.

id.description: The supervisor's id, from their token.

name.description: Their display name, when the token carried one.

ToolSpec.description: What the app declares about one tool: the contract the model sees and the rules the platform enforces before running it.

name.description: The name the model calls, unique within the agent: find_patient, book_slot.

description.description: What the tool does, as the model reads it. In the app this is the method's docstring.

parameters.description: The arguments, as a JSON Schema object the model must satisfy.

side_effect.description: read looks at the world; write changes it and can be undone; irreversible changes it for good, so the platform asks the caller first. Absent means read.

confirm.description: The read-back the agent says before the tool runs, with {argument} placeholders filled from the call: 'Le reservo con la doctora {doctor} el {at}. ¿Confirmo?'. Absent means no confirmation.

pii.description: Argument names that carry personal data, masked in the log by declaration.

timeout_s.description: How long the platform waits for the app's result before reporting an error to the model, in seconds.

ToolResult.description: What came back from running a tool in the app's process. Either an output or an error, never both.

call_id.description: The id the tool.call carried, so the result finds its call.

name.description: The tool's name, repeated so a log line stands on its own.

output.description: Whatever the method returned, as JSON. Absent when the tool failed.

error.description: What went wrong, in words the model may read. Absent when the tool succeeded.

summary.description: A one-line version of the output for the console and for memory, when the app wrote one.

duration_s.description: How long the app's method took, in seconds.

MemoryFact.description: One thing remembered about a contact: a sentence, where it came from, and how well it matched when recalled.

id.description: The fact's id in the memory store.

text.description: The fact itself, as one sentence: 'prefers mornings', 'allergic to penicillin'.

category.description: The tenant's own word for what kind of fact this is, from its memory.remember list: 'alergias', 'preference'.

score.description: How well it matched the recall query, 0 to 1. Absent when remembering, which has no query.

source.description: The call this fact was extracted from, when known.

MemoryOp.description: One operation against the contact's memory: a recall during the turn, a remember at hangup, or a forget on request.

op.description: recall reads facts for the turn; remember writes facts extracted at hangup; forget erases on the contact's request.

contact.description: The contact id the memory belongs to.

query.description: What was asked of memory, for a recall.

facts.description: The facts read, written or erased.

took_ms.description: How long the operation took, in milliseconds. A recall in the turn must stay under 150.

DocSource.description: One chunk of the knowledge base that retrieval put in front of the model for this turn.

id.description: The chunk's id in the knowledge store.

path.description: The document the chunk came from, as the tenant pushed it: 'faq/horarios.md'.

heading.description: The heading the chunk sits under, since chunks are cut by heading.

score.description: The fused rank score (vector and BM25 through RRF), higher is better.

excerpt.description: The chunk's text as the model read it, the body under its heading: the log carries the evidence an answer had to come from, so a judge reading it afterwards can find it.

CostRate.description: The exchange rate the cost was computed with, stated so the number can be reproduced.

currency.description: Costs are always stated in euros.

usd_to_eur.description: How many euros one US dollar bought, since providers price in dollars.

as_of.description: The day the rate is from, as YYYY-MM-DD.

CostRow.description: One priced line: a model, what was counted, how much, and what it came to.

provider.description: The provider, as the usage row names it: anthropic, elevenlabs, soniox.

model.description: The model, as the usage row names it.

unit.description: What the provider bills by for this line.

quantity.description: How many of that unit the call used.

unit_price_usd.description: The provider's list price per unit, in US dollars, from the price table.

eur.description: quantity times unit_price_usd times the rate, in euros.

UnpricedRow.description: A usage row the price table does not know. It is listed, never priced at zero.

provider.description: The provider of the row nobody could price.

model.description: The model of the row nobody could price.

Cost.description: What the call cost in provider fees, informational, in euros. The runtime never prices commercially; this is the provider's bill as best we know it.

eur.description: The sum of every priced row, in euros.

rows.description: Every usage row that had a price, one line per unit billed.

unpriced.description: The usage rows the price table did not know, so the total is known to be incomplete.

VoiceConfig.description: Which voice speaks for the agent: the name it was asked for, or the id the provider knows it by.

name.description: The voice as the app wrote it: one of the platform's curated names, or a provider's own id. Resolved to a provider and an id when the app declares itself, so an unknown name is refused there and never at the first utterance.

provider.description: The TTS provider: elevenlabs. Absent when the curated name decides it.

model.description: The provider's model, when the default is not wanted.

voice_id.description: The provider's id for the voice.

ModelConfig.description: Which model does a job (the LLM, or the STT), and the one or two knobs worth turning.

provider.description: The provider: anthropic, openai, soniox, deepgram.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, for an LLM. Absent means the provider's default.

TurnConfig.description: How the session decides that the caller has finished, and when the caller may interrupt.

min_interruption_words.description: How many words the caller must say before the agent stops talking. Guards against 'mm-hm'.

endpointing_ms.description: How long a silence, in milliseconds, before the turn detector is asked whether the caller is done.

Pronunciation.description: How the voice says one word it would otherwise get wrong: a proper name, a brand, a street.

word.description: The word as the model writes it: Vidal.

spoken.description: What the voice is given instead: bidál. Applied to the reply before it is spoken, never to the log.

StateFieldSpec.description: What the app declares about one field of its state: who may see it. A field never declared is tenant.

name.description: The field's name in the app's state, as state.set sends it: patient, slots.

EventSpec.description: One outside event the agent accepts, and from whom. An event nobody declared is refused before it touches the log.

name.description: The event's name, dotted, as call.event or pinecall.event will send it: slot.released, form.submitted.

from.description: Who may send it: the tenant's backend, a participant's browser, or both.

KnowledgeFile.description: One file of knowledge, sent whole: its path as the tenant keeps it, and its text.

path.description: The file's path as the tenant keeps it, relative to the agent: 'knowledge/clinica.md', 'faq/horarios.md'.

text.description: The file's whole text, as the app read it from disk.

DocsConfig.description: The knowledge base the agent answers from, and how its chunks reach the model. It is named by the base it was pushed under, with PUT /v1/knowledge/{base}.

base.description: The base's name, the one it was pushed to with PUT /v1/knowledge/{base}: 'clinica-norte'.

k.description: How many chunks a turn's retrieval puts in front of the model at most.

min_score.description: The fused rank score a chunk must reach to be put in front of the model. Absent, nothing is dropped from the top k.

MemoryConfig.description: What memory keeps about a contact across calls, and what it must never keep. Both lists are in the tenant's own words.

remember.description: The kinds of fact worth keeping, as the tenant names them: 'alergias', 'preference', 'pets'. They become the categories remember extracts and recall reads back.

forget.description: The kinds of fact that are never written, whatever the call said: 'card_numbers', 'diagnosis'. Dropped before they touch the store.

AgentConfig.description: What an app declares about its agent: the voice, the models, the language, the greeting, the tools, and who may see and send what. Every field is optional so a configure can change one thing.

prompt.description: The blocks of the prompt in the one order they are sent: every static block, then the history, then every dynamic block. Absent, the layout is the default: identity · knowledge · tools, the history, view.

language.description: The language the agent speaks and expects, as a BCP 47 tag: es-ES, es-UY.

greeting.description: What the agent says first, verbatim, when a call starts.

says.description: How the voice says the words it would otherwise get wrong. Applied to the reply on its way to the TTS.

hears.description: The words the ears must know: the agent's own name, the doctors', the streets. Given to the STT as keyterms.

knowledge.description: The one file the agent knows by heart, sent whole: the bridge reads it beside the class and the runtime puts its text in the static block, once per call.

docs.description: The knowledge base the agent answers from, by the name it was pushed under, and how its chunks reach the model.

memory.description: What memory keeps about a contact across calls, in the tenant's words, and what it must never keep.

tools.description: Every tool the agent may ever see. Which ones are visible now is tools.set.

state_fields.description: Who may see each field of the app's state. A field not listed is tenant: seen by the tenant's readers, never by the public.

events.description: The outside events this agent accepts and from whom. Anything else is refused before it touches the log.
